ok so I finally saw Gladiator II and I have thoughts. Did it live up to the hype? Sort of. Mostly no. But I had a good time, so I'm confused too.

First, the good: Denzel. Holy crap. Every scene he's in, the movie wakes up. He's clearly having a blast playing Macrinus, all scheming and charm, and he walks away with the whole thing. Paul Mescal is solid and has the presence, but he's playing the quiet brooding guy, and when he's next to Denzel it's like watching someone bring a acoustic guitar to a Metallica show. The arena stuff is also just fun. The rhino, the baboons, the flooded Colosseum with the ships. Is it historically ridiculous? Absolutely. Do I care? Not when it's on a giant screen.

Now the bad. The plot is basically the first movie with the names swapped. Slave-turned-gladiator, corrupt emperors, a Rome-needs-saving speech, a mentor figure who may or may not make it. I kept waiting for it to surprise me and it never did. The first one worked because Maximus's revenge felt personal and the stakes were simple. Here the emotional hook is "my mom is Lucilla and there are Secrets," and it just didn't land for me. Pedro Pascal is great too, but I felt like he deserved a bigger part to play.

And look, I know the original came out in 2000 and nobody could realistically top it, but the movie never seems to decide if it wants to be a loving follow-up or its own thing. It ends up being a really expensive cover version.

So 7/10. Entertaining, and Denzel is worth the ticket alone, but the hype had me expecting an all-timer and what I got was a pretty good Saturday night movie. Anyone else feel this way or am I being too harsh?

Short version: yeah, it mostly lived up to the hype, but not in the way I expected.

The good stuff first. The scale is ridiculous. The first time the sandworms show up in action I actually said "holy crap" out loud in a quiet theater, and the guy next to me nodded like we'd just survived something together. The black-and-white arena sequence on Giedi Prime might be my favorite thing in the whole movie. Austin Butler as Feyd was unhinged in the best way, and I kinda wish he had more screen time. And the sound design?? Zimmer needs to be studied. My chest was vibrating for like two hours.

Now the stuff people are gonna yell at me for. The middle drags a bit. I get that they're building Paul's slide into messiah territory, but there were a couple stretches where I checked out. Also, Zendaya is barely in this for the amount she was marketed, and Chani deserved more to do than stare meaningfully at the horizon. Her ending hit hard though, and honestly it's the thing that elevated the whole last act for me. People who just wanted a victory lap for Paul clearly missed the point. He's NOT the hero here, and the movie makes that pretty uncomfortably clear.

Is it better than the first one? Ehh, I think it's a tie. Part One is tighter, Part Two is bigger and messier but swings harder. If you loved the first, you'll be fine. If the first one bored you, this won't convert you.

8.5/10, would watch again on the biggest screen possible. Don't wait for streaming on this one, you'll be cheating yourself.

Anyone else feel like the ending was way more bleak than people are admitting?

So we go to that little bar by the laundromat, the one with the weird fish tank. And we're fine, we're having a nice time. Then her coworker Dennis shows up. You haven't met Dennis. Dennis is a lot. He's the kind of guy who says "bro" to women and means it as a compliment. And he's got three friends with him, and suddenly we're at a table of seven people and somebody's ordering shots for the whole table.

And I'm like, no, no, I'm good, and then I'm holding a shot. I don't even know how it got there. It's just in my hand.

So that's whatever, that's fine, but then Dennis says there's a thing, a party, like a "you have to see this place" party. And I swear to god, Priya and I look at each other and we both go, "ugh, fine." Because we're idiots. So we pile into an Uber, and it's like six of us in a car meant for four, and I'm basically sitting on the gear shift, and the driver is just staring straight ahead like he's seen things.

We get to this place, and it is not a party. It's a guy's apartment, and the guy is making soup. At eleven at night. Big pot of soup, a bunch of people standing around in the kitchen, and nobody can explain why. I asked, and the guy goes, "It's a soup night." Like that's a thing! Like I'm the weird one for not knowing!

Honestly, the soup was good, I'm not gonna lie. But then it gets worse, because someone brings out a karaoke machine. And Dennis, of course, grabs the mic and does this whole Bon Jovi thing, and the neighbor, this poor woman in a bathrobe, bangs on the door. And instead of, you know, turning it down, the soup guy invites her in. So now she's got a bowl of soup and she's doing "Total Eclipse of the Heart." And she was amazing, I'm not even kidding, she kind of saved the night.

But that's not even the sideways part. The sideways part is when I go to leave and realize I don't have my phone. Nowhere. I check my pockets, I check the couch, I'm basically tearing apart this guy's apartment while there's a woman in a bathrobe belting out Bonnie Tyler. And Priya's like, "Just call it," and I'm like, "With WHAT?"

So we call it from her phone, and we hear it ringing, and it's coming from the pot of soup. Okay, not in the pot. Next to the pot. But Dennis had put his jacket over it, and honestly I will never forget that moment, all of us just staring at a jacket that's ringing.

Anyway, I got home at like three. Priya says she'll never speak to me again, which, she was the one who said one drink! And now I smell like soup. That's the whole story. I'm never going out again.
